title: Your First App: Hello World
summary: Edit the starter app and show your own message on the screen.
heading: Your First App: Hello World

blocks.text: After ng new and ng serve (Chapter 15), you saw a starter page in the browser. That page is one component — the root component, App. Let's open it and make it say hello our way.
The root component is two files that work together: the class (the data and logic) and the template (the HTML it shows).

blocks.label: app.ts (the class)

blocks.text: The class has a property title. The template reads it with {{ title }} — the interpolation from Chapter 6. Angular renders the root component into the <app-root> tag inside index.html, and that's what you see.
Edit the code below and press Run. Change the username value, or the text in the template, and watch the output update.

blocks.html:
Hello, {{ username }}!

Welcome to your first Angular app.

blocks.text: Change username = 'World' to your own name and press Run — the heading updates, because the template just shows whatever the class holds.

items: The starter app is a single root component, App.
A component is a class (data) plus a template (HTML).
{{ title }} shows a class property on the page.
Angular renders the root component into <app-root> in index.html.
Change the class value and the screen follows.
